relations.evidence: In general, if any operand evaluates to a `MISSING` value, the enclosing operator will return `MISSING`; if none of the operands evaluates to a `MISSING` value but there is an operand which evaluates to a `NULL` value, the enclosing operator will return `NULL`.

notable_absence.finding: Unlike introduction.md and 1_intro.md, this grammar-detail page never once mentions SQL++ for Query, N1QL, or draws any comparison to Couchbase's other dialect - it is written as a self-contained language reference. Per the round's dialect warning, that absence of a stated equivalence is itself the reason every construct here (operator precedence table, MISSING/NULL comparison rules, quantified-expression EVERY/SOME AND EVERY distinction) was minted under analytics: rather than reused from n1ql:, even where an n1ql:* sibling construct probably exists: this page gives no textual license to fold them.
